description: tshark command examples for Vectra detection PCAP triage — ATT&CK-aligned hunting, credential / lateral-movement / C2 / exfil pivots, and recovery-driven validation.

commands.purpose: Validate tshark version/build before running filters
commands.command: tshark -v
commands.notes: Use first to interpret dissector and field behavior differences across versions

commands.command: sha256sum capture.pcap
commands.notes: Preserve chain-of-custody context. fetch-detection-pcap.sh prints this automatically when it decodes the MCP payload.

commands.purpose: Check protocol hierarchy and capture sanity
commands.command: tshark -r capture.pcap -q -z io,phs
commands.notes: Quickly reveals protocol mix and helps pick the right investigation path.

commands.purpose: Validate key DNS / SMB / HTTP / TLS fields
commands.command: tshark -G fields | grep -E "(dns\.qry\.name|smb2\.cmd|http\.request\.uri|tls\.handshake)"
commands.notes: Preflight check to avoid failed commands on missing dissectors or field names.

commands.command: tshark -G fields | grep -E "(kerberos\.|ldap\.|ntlmssp\.|smb2\.nt_status)"
commands.notes: Confirms support for credential and lateral-movement pivots.

commands.command: tshark -r capture.pcap -Y "tls.handshake.type == 1"
commands.notes: Primary pivot for TLS client fingerprinting and beacon shape.

commands.purpose: Export TLS tuple + SNI + ALPN + cipher fields
commands.command: tshark -r capture.pcap -Y "tls.handshake.type == 1" -T fields -E header=y -e frame.number -e ip.src -e ip.dst -e tcp.srcport -e tcp.dstport -e tls.handshake.version -e tls.handshake.ciphersuite -e tls.handshake.extensions_server_name -e tls.handshake.extensions_alpn_str
commands.notes: Core TLS triage row — what host talks to what destination over which TLS variant, plus the SNI and ALPN.

commands.command: tshark -r capture.pcap -Y "tls.handshake.type == 1" -T fields -e ip.src -e ip.dst -e tls.handshake.ja3 | sort | uniq -c | sort -rn
commands.notes: Always-available client TLS fingerprint. Useful for spotting non-browser clients.

commands.command: tshark -r capture.pcap -Y "tls.handshake.type == 11" -T fields -e ip.src -e ip.dst -e x509ce.subject -e x509ce.subjectAltName_element
commands.notes: Surface CN / SAN values when the full handshake is captured.

commands.purpose: Count TLS Client Hellos by source
commands.command: tshark -r capture.pcap -Y "tls.handshake.type == 1" -T fields -e ip.src | sort | uniq -c | sort -rn
commands.notes: Detect potential beaconing or staged C2 check-ins.

commands.purpose: Summarize SYN-only activity for scan/beacon detection
commands.command: tshark -r capture.pcap -Y "tcp.flags.syn == 1 and tcp.flags.ack == 0" -T fields -e ip.src -e ip.dst -e tcp.dstport | sort | uniq -c | sort -rn
commands.notes: High repeat or high fan-out patterns can indicate reconnaissance or C2 retries.

commands.command: tshark -r capture.pcap -q -z conv,tcp
commands.notes: Helps surface persistent C2 channels worth pivoting from.

commands.purpose: Extract DNS queries with core context
commands.command: tshark -r capture.pcap -Y "dns.flags.response == 0" -T fields -E header=y -e frame.time -e ip.src -e dns.qry.type -e dns.qry.name
commands.notes: Triage suspicious DNS behavior and identify pivots.

commands.purpose: Detect long / high-entropy DNS query names
commands.command: tshark -r capture.pcap -Y "dns.flags.response == 0 && dns.qry.name matches \"[A-Za-z0-9]{25,}\"" -T fields -e frame.time -e ip.src -e dns.qry.name
commands.notes: Identify possible DNS tunneling patterns.

commands.command: tshark -r capture.pcap -Y "dns.flags.response == 0 && dns.qry.type == 16" -T fields -e frame.time -e ip.src -e dns.qry.name
commands.notes: Useful for payload-bearing TXT abuse checks.

commands.command: tshark -r capture.pcap -Y "smb2" -T fields -E header=y -e frame.time -e ip.src -e ip.dst -e smb2.cmd -e smb2.tree -e smb2.share_name
commands.notes: Supports lateral movement triage. Watch for ADMIN$ / C$ / IPC$.

commands.command: tshark -r capture.pcap -Y "smb2 && smb2.nt_status" -T fields -e frame.time -e ip.src -e ip.dst -e smb2.nt_status
commands.notes: Identifies likely invalid-credential and brute-force behavior over SMB.

commands.command: tshark -r capture.pcap -Y "tcp.port==445" -T fields -e ip.src -e ip.dst | sort | uniq -c | sort -rn
commands.notes: Use when SMB dissector fields are missing.

commands.command: tshark -r capture.pcap -Y "tcp.port==3389" -T fields -E header=y -e frame.time -e ip.src -e ip.dst -e tcp.srcport -e tcp.dstport
commands.notes: Supports RDP lateral-movement investigations.

commands.command: tshark -r capture.pcap -Y "kerberos.msg_type" -T fields -e frame.time -e ip.src -e ip.dst -e kerberos.msg_type -e kerberos.CNameString -e kerberos.SNameString
commands.notes: Surfaces account/service targeting and ticket flow anomalies.

commands.command: tshark -r capture.pcap -Y "kerberos.error_code" -T fields -e ip.src -e kerberos.error_code | sort | uniq -c | sort -rn
commands.notes: Spikes can indicate password spray / AS-REP roasting / service account misuse.

commands.command: tshark -r capture.pcap -Y "ldap" -T fields -e frame.time -e ip.src -e ip.dst -e ldap.protocolOp
commands.notes: Highlights suspicious bind/search operations against directory services.

commands.command: tshark -r capture.pcap -Y "ntlmssp" -T fields -e frame.time -e ip.src -e ip.dst -e ntlmssp.auth.username -e ntlmssp.auth.domain -e ntlmssp.negotiate.callingworkstation -e ntlmssp.challenge.target_name
commands.notes: Surface account, source workstation, and target server for any NTLM exchange.

commands.command: tshark -r capture.pcap -Y "tcp.port==5985 || tcp.port==5986" -T fields -e frame.time -e ip.src -e ip.dst -e tcp.dstport
commands.notes: Supports hands-on-keyboard lateral-movement scoping.

commands.command: tshark -r capture.pcap -Y "http.request.method" -T fields -E header=y -e frame.time -e ip.src -e ip.dst -e http.host -e http.request.method -e http.request.uri -e http.user_agent
commands.notes: Captures request observables for web and exfil triage.

commands.command: tshark -r capture.pcap -Y "http.request.method == \"POST\" && http.content_length > 500000" -T fields -e frame.time -e ip.src -e ip.dst -e http.host -e http.request.uri -e http.content_length
commands.notes: Potential bulk upload / exfil behavior.

commands.command: tshark -r capture.pcap -Y "http.user_agent" -T fields -e http.user_agent | sort | uniq -c | sort -rn | head -50
commands.notes: Flags scripted tooling and unusual client signatures.

commands.purpose: Surface HTTP requests with Authorization headers
commands.command: tshark -r capture.pcap -Y "http.authorization || http.authbasic" -T fields -e frame.time -e ip.src -e ip.dst -e http.host -e http.request.method -e http.request.uri -e http.user_agent
commands.notes: Capture credentialed HTTP — useful for staging endpoint, internal tool, or proxied auth review.

commands.command: tshark -r capture.pcap -Y "tls.handshake.type == 1" -T json
commands.notes: Machine-readable output for jq / Python enrichment chains.
